content: 1. Fezolinetant: Conjugated synthetic estrogens increase the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 2. CYP1A2 Inhibitors: Drugs that are weak, moderate, or strong inhibitors of CYP1A2 (e.g., ospemifene) increase the area under the curve (AUC) and peak plasma concentration of fezolinetant. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Anastrozole: Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated as estrogens may diminish the pharmacologic action of anastrozole. 4. Antithrombin Alfa and Antithrombin III: Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of these agents through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Apalutamide: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Argatroban, Bivalirudin, Dalteparin, Enoxaparin, Fondaparinux, Heparin, and Bemiparin: Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of these anticoagulants through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. These combinations are contraindicated. 7. Carbamazepine: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Cimetidine, Clarithromycin, and Erythromycin: These drugs increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. St. John’s Wort: This herbal supplement decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Tucatinib: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates if unavoidable. 11. Antidiabetics (e.g., Albiglutide, Exenatide, Insulin): Conjugated synthetic estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic agents. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 12. Antibiotics (e.g., Amikacin, Azithromycin, Ciprofloxacin): These drugs may decrease the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 13. Antifungals (e.g., Fluconazole, Ketoconazole): These drugs increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Corticosteroids (e.g., Dexamethasone, Hydrocortisone): These drugs decrease the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Cyclosporine: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor. 16. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Griseofulvin: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Hemins: Conjugated synthetic estrogens reduce the effects of hemins through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Hylauronidase: Estrogens in large systemic doses may render tissues partially resistant to hyaluronidase, requiring larger amounts of the enzyme for equivalent effects. Use caution and monitor. 20. Iloperidone: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Indinavir: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor. 22. Itraconazole: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. DHEA (Herbal): This supplement increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Diltiazem: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Dronedarone: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor. 26. Efavirenz: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Elagolix: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor and adjust the dose of CYP3A substrates as needed. 28. Encorafenib: This drug both inhibits and induces CYP3A4, potentially altering the levels of conjugated synthetic estrogens. Use caution and monitor. 29. Fosfomycin: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 30. Fosaprepitant: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 31. Gentamicin: This drug decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 32. Istradefylline: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Ketoconazole: This drug increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Use caution and monitor. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when conjugated synthetic estrogens are coadministered with other medications.
